question.text: When evaluating AIF fund terms, the 'management fee offset' provision benefits investors by:

answer.text: Increasing the management fee to provide better service
Allowing investors to pay management fees in installments
Reducing the management fee by the amount of transaction fees, monitoring fees, or other fees collected by the GP from portfolio companies
Exempting investors from paying any fees

explanation.text: The Logic: A "management fee offset" provision (an industry term in PE/AIF fund documents) reduces the management fee otherwise owed by investors by all or part of the transaction, monitoring, director, or similar fees that the GP collects from portfolio companies. The economic effect is to reduce double-counting of GP compensation. The Trap: The offset reduces, not increases, net fees. It is not about payment timing or about exempting investors from fees altogether. Note: The XIX-A workbook covers management fees, expenses, additional returns/carry, investor negotiation of fee terms, and PPM-audit review of fee structures; it does not specifically define "management fee offset" as a defined term. Treat this as general PE fund-terms knowledge.
